data.turoyo: Azza i Zarife aʕme. Kul walay kəzza sap pašawiye, kəmraǧyo, lo qoṭəʕ hol d azzən lu Qars qm u Gawar.
data.translation: Särîfe aber zog mit ihnen, und in jeder Stadt, wohin sie kam, flehte sie den jeweiligen Statthalter an, aber sie drang mit ihren Bitten nicht durch, bis sie nach Kars gelangten an der Grenze der Russen.

rationale: First Infectum box: feminine iterative narrative with governor addressees.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (96/223)

data.turoyo: Omər l Nari məlle: "Gəmraǧeno m aloho w bəṯr menux, ya u zaboṭo di gammiyaṯi, kəbʕeno d obatli ḥšara w ʕlama, be l mə zbəṭlux i gammiyaṯi!"
data.translation: Nari sprach: O du, der du dieses Schifffesthältst, ich bitte Gott und dich, daß du mir ein Zeichen gibst, warum du dieses Schifffestgehalten hast! -

data.turoyo: Mraǧele l abre du hərč, lə ṭrele d qoṭəʕ qarʕe.
data.translation: Aber der Sohn des Bären bat für ihn und liess nicht zu, dass er ihm den Kopf abhieb.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (101/31)

data.turoyo: Mraǧele mene, omər: “Kanne ad dayne w ad dafetir di ḥkume kulle b qḏoli, kobaʕno d ṭoratli l ṣafrayto, d maslamno ad dafetir di ḥkume w ad dayne, ahlan w sahlan, mə d kəbʕat, səm ebi.”
data.translation: Der Wali bat ihn: Die Schulden und die Akten der Regierung liegen mir alle auf dem Hals. Laß mich bitte noch bis Morgen los, damit ich die Akten der Regierung und die Schulden übergeben kann! Dann magst du gerne kommen und mit mir tun, was du willst. -

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: unambiguous mene marks the petitioned person.

data.translation: They begged me: ‘For God’s sake and yours, tell him to perform magic for us; I had a fiancée whom they took away from me...’ <...>

summary: m- marks the petitioned person in96/223,101/31,112/95,160. In PrS63/75 the postverbal l-NP denotes the agent, while PrS68/29 u taʕlo denotes the person whose release is requested; these roles must not be conflated.
Infectum supplies iterative past pleading, first-person requests and request content with d-. These are all bitten, not separate senses for intercession or praying.

Read-only trǧy lookup confirms reciprocal cross-references already exist. Both paradigms share petitioning and m- government; the t-less forms remain rǧy II. The reader's suggestion that a cross-reference is missing is not applicable.
PrS68/29 duplicates the inherited prs193/34 wording; do not add the same fox-release example.
b heviye w b rəǧa intensifies the request; the verb remains a lexical petitioning verb, and no independent light-verb idiom is established.
Round 1 already added II Infectum. Reader claims of its absence are stale. Infectum-wa is the only new box supplied here.
Requests concerning hospitality, magic, votes, service time and a name-register assignment remain bitten. Their requested actions do not establish separate senses or light-verb idioms.
The t-less mraǧ- forms remain rǧy II, preserving the inherited trǧy cross-reference. The new material alone does not justify merging roots.
Is gmarǧeno at112/160 a variant of rǧy II with vowel/consonant ordering variation, or a reduction of trǧy I? Retained provisionally under II, without inventing a new paradigm.
Should the editors expand the existing reciprocal cross-references into a note explaining the relationship of the t-less II and t-retaining I paradigms?
Confirm that mraǧele u taʕlo requests the fox's release rather than addressing the fox; context and marfalle strongly favor the beneficiary reading.
Confirm mraǧanwo and mraǧən plural vocalism, and whether l- in Jan 3.17/289 is a normal addressee alternative to m- rather than a special respectful title construction.
m- addressee and d-request content recur; Jan 3.17/289 also has l-marked episcopal addressee. Agent l-NPs in round 1 must not be conflated with this latter role.
